messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: entropy-based simplex prior?
parts:
I'm looking to construct a prior on K-simplexes theta
(theta[k] > 0, sum(theta) = 1) that favors low
entropy theta. The context is a genomics model of
RNA splice variation, where there are often 1000s
of possibilities, but only a handful that are non-zero.
The Dirichlet's not quite right here.

I was about to mail out a suggestion for a prior on
simplexes I dreamed up,

p(theta) propto exp(alpha * H[theta])

when I did some searches online and came across this
arXiv paper of Matt's, which introduces the exact
same distribution for the same reasons:

http://arxiv.org/pdf/1009.5761.pdf

Did you (Matt) invent this or are there other refs? I
found Rodriguez on "entropic priors", but the motivation is
very max-entropy motivated, and I couldn't line up the ideas.

The alpha term is nice because at 0, it reverts to the uniform
distribution over simplex, if it's positive then you prefer
high entropy and if it's negative you prefer low entropy.
Because the simplex is compact and the H[theta] for a K-simplex
theta is bounded between 0 and K, I think it all normalizes
properly.

Should we add this to Stan? I think it'd be super-cool if Matt
invented the prior so that we could write it as:

theta ~ hoffman(alpha);

I was very pleased with myself for coming up with the alpha bit,
and I could being doing much worse than replicating thoughts Matt
had a few years ago!

- Bob

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] entropy-based simplex prior?
parts:
I believe Skilling uses a similar approach for his maximum entropy deconvolution. See Sivia's book "Data Analysis" which goes through the motivation and has references.

Incidentally, did the Dirichlet not work with alpha << 1? That induces some serious sparsity.

messages.author: 1004dd6f66bb10c3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] entropy-based simplex prior?
parts:
It would be super-cool if I'd invented it, but I definitely didn't!
There's a small literature on using these to introduce sparsity in for
audio source separation models, which I believe starts here:
http://www.cs.illinois.edu/~paris/Paris_Smaragdis_page/Paris_Smaragdis_Publications_files/smaragdis-icassp2008.pdf
They reference Matt Brand's paper from 1999:
http://www.merl.com/publications/docs/TR98-18.pdf

I'd second Michael's question about the Dirichlet, though. My
understanding is that the primary reason people prefer the entropic
prior is that it doesn't introduce degeneracies in MAP estimation like
the Dirichlet does.

Matt
